newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Key elections in El Salvador off to calm start.
newsitem.headline: Key elections in El Salvador off to calm start.

text.p: Salvadorans voted on Sunday in key nationwide elections to renew Congress and elect 262 mayors in races that pitted former battlefield enemies at the polls.
Voting started in an atmosphere of calm under the watchful eye of about 10,000 police and 1,000 international observers.
About 2.6 million voters were eligible to choose from among 13 parties to fill positions for 84 deputies in Congress and for 262 mayors.
Analysts said the elections are key, as they could strip away power from the ruling right-wing National Republican Alliance (ARENA).
Pitted against ARENA are the former guerrillas of the left-wing Farabundo Marti Liberation Movement (FMLN), which has gained support at the expense of the ARENA.
The FMLN has transformed itself from a guerrilla movement into a democratic party and hopes to make gains on the 20 seats they now hold in Congress, compared with ARENA's 39 seats.
"We hope that the people will massively turn out and take advantage of the moment to express their opinion," El Salvador President Armando Calderon Sol told reporters after voting in the capital.
Various opinion polls have shown a decline in support for ARENA, which Calderon Sols represents.

Two opinion polls from local universities, and another from the Gallup organisation, showed the FMLN was slightly ahead in voter support, although the number of voters who planned to abstain was high.
In the 12-year civil war that ended with a peace treaty in January 1992, about 75,000 people were killed.
